title: 2nd Stopping Place 2nd Truth 3rd Example From Sura Al Nahl And The General Conclusion

questions.question: Which two fruits does the passage tell us to think about carefully?
questions.answer: Dates and grapes.

questions.question: What do these two fruits help show to smart people?
questions.answer: They show Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What kinds of food and drink do these fruits give people?
questions.answer: They give fresh food, dried food, and sweet things to eat and drink.

questions.question: What is surprising about where these plants grow?
questions.answer: They grow in very dry ground with little water.

questions.question: What comparison is used for these fruit plants?
questions.answer: They are compared to a factory or a machine making sweet food.

questions.question: About how thick is one vine branch in the example?
questions.answer: It is about as thick as a finger.

questions.question: About how many grape clusters can one branch hold in the example?
questions.answer: About twenty.

questions.question: What is inside each cluster in great number?
questions.answer: Many grapes.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the outside of each grape?
questions.answer: It has a thin, delicate, colorful skin.

questions.question: What is inside the grape that points to planning?
questions.answer: Seeds with hard shells.

questions.question: Why does the passage say blind forces and nature cannot make this?
questions.answer: Because this work is too careful, wise, and balanced.

questions.question: If the same careful fruit is made all over the earth in the same way, what does that prove?
questions.answer: It proves one Creator made them all.

questions.question: What do the many works in these verses together say about Allah?
questions.answer: They all point to Allah alone.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the third verse in this passage?
questions.answer: Dates and grapes are signs that teach about Allah.

questions.question: Who benefits from thinking deeply about these signs?
questions.answer: People who use their minds.

questions.question: How are date palms and grapevines special even before we eat their fruit?
questions.answer: They grow in hard, dry places and still make rich food.

questions.question: What does that tell us about their Maker?
questions.answer: Their Maker has great power and wisdom.

questions.question: What might a thinking person say after seeing these fruits?
questions.answer: The One who made them can make the whole universe.

questions.question: Why is one grape branch used as an example?
questions.answer: To show a lot of amazing work in a small thing.

questions.question: What does the passage say each grape is like when it gives sweet juice?
questions.answer: Like a tiny pump.

questions.question: Why is the grape’s skin important in the example?
questions.answer: It protects the fruit in a careful way.

questions.question: Why are the seeds important in the example?
questions.answer: They keep what is needed for the next life of the plant.

questions.question: What makes the making of grapes more amazing than just one plant?
questions.answer: The same work happens across the whole earth.

questions.question: What does doing this at the same time and in the same way show?
questions.answer: It shows one Lord is in control.

questions.question: What things are said to have no share in this work?
questions.answer: Chance, blind forces, nature, and causes.

questions.question: What small job is left for those created things?
questions.answer: They only serve as tools under Allah’s command.

questions.question: How do the three verses work together in the passage?
questions.answer: Together they all witness Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Which fruits are named as signs in this part of the text?
questions.answer: Dates and grapes.

questions.question: What do people make from them according to the passage’s meaning?
questions.answer: Sweet things and good food.

questions.question: Why does the passage call them signs?
questions.answer: Because they help people know Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What is unusual about the land where these plants stand?
questions.answer: It is sandy and dry.

questions.question: If delicious fruit comes from dry ground, what can we understand?
questions.answer: Allah can bring wonderful things from hard places.

questions.question: What does the passage compare the fruit trees to?
questions.answer: To places and tools that make sweet food.

questions.question: When a person sees such careful making, what big idea should he understand?
questions.answer: The Maker of these fruits made everything.

questions.question: What number of grape bunches is given for one branch?
questions.answer: Twenty bunches.

questions.question: What does each bunch have many of?
questions.answer: Sugary grapes.

questions.question: Name one careful feature on the outside of a grape.
questions.answer: Its thin colorful covering.

questions.question: Name one careful feature inside a grape.
questions.answer: Its hard-covered seeds.

questions.question: Why are these details important for understanding the passage?
questions.answer: They show care, order, and wisdom.

questions.question: What kind of makers are rejected by the passage?
questions.answer: Mindless and messy forces.

questions.question: Why are they rejected?
questions.answer: Because they cannot make something so exact and balanced.

questions.question: What final truth do the many signs and works agree on?
questions.answer: That Allah is One.

questions.question: In this passage, what are children and grown-ups asked to notice in dates and grapes?
questions.answer: Proof of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Are these fruits shown as plain and simple only, or as full of careful design?
questions.answer: They are shown as full of careful design.

questions.question: What are some good things people get from these fruits?
questions.answer: Nourishment and sweet foods.

questions.question: What kind of place do these plants grow in?
questions.answer: Dry soil and sandy land.

questions.question: Why does growing there make them a wonder?
questions.answer: Because rich fruit comes from a hard place.

questions.question: What does the passage say a vine branch can carry?
questions.answer: Many bunches of grapes.

questions.question: What does this teach about small things?
questions.answer: Even small things can hold great wonders.

questions.question: How is a single grape described by its job?
questions.answer: It gives out sweet juice.

questions.question: What protects the grape on the outside?
questions.answer: A very thin skin.

questions.question: What inside the grape points to memory and future growth?
questions.answer: The seeds.

questions.question: If the same kind of grapes are made everywhere with the same wisdom, what can we infer?
questions.answer: One Creator is making them all.

questions.question: Why can’t random events be the real maker of this fruit?
questions.answer: Because random events do not plan wisely.

questions.question: What role do nature and causes have, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are only used as helpers under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What do all these examples say with one voice?
questions.answer: Allah alone is the Lord.

questions.question: What fruit example is the third one in this passage?
questions.answer: The example of dates and grapes.

questions.question: What does the passage say intelligent people can find in them?
questions.answer: Clear evidence of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Besides fresh fruit, what other kinds of benefit come from them?
questions.answer: Dried fruit and other sweet foods.

questions.question: What does the passage want us to notice about the place where they grow?
questions.answer: The place is dry, yet the fruit is rich and sweet.

questions.question: What does that show about Allah’s work?
questions.answer: It shows amazing power and wisdom.

questions.question: What picture is given to help us imagine how these plants work?
questions.answer: They are like sweet-making factories.

questions.question: How many clusters are pictured on one branch?
questions.answer: Twenty.

questions.question: What does the large number of grapes on one branch show?
questions.answer: It shows generosity and careful creating.

questions.question: What is one special thing about the grape’s covering?
questions.answer: It is thin and delicate.

questions.question: What is one special thing about the grape’s center?
questions.answer: It has seeds prepared for new life.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention grapes across the whole earth?
questions.answer: To show the same art appears everywhere.

questions.question: What does doing the same art everywhere prove?
questions.answer: It proves the Creator of all is one.

questions.question: Can blind forces reach this careful work as true makers?
questions.answer: No, they cannot be the true makers.

questions.question: Why not?
questions.answer: Because the work is too balanced, skilled, and wise.

questions.question: What do the many lordly works together testify to?
questions.answer: They testify to the unity of Allah.

questions.question: What two plants are used to teach a lesson in this section?
questions.answer: The date palm and the grapevine.

questions.question: What lesson do they teach?
questions.answer: They teach that Allah is One.

questions.question: Who is especially invited to understand this lesson?
questions.answer: People who think with intelligence.

questions.question: What makes these fruits amazing where they grow?
questions.answer: They grow in dry, thirsty land.

questions.question: What does the sweetness of the fruit tell us about its Creator?
questions.answer: He gives rich blessings with wisdom and power.

questions.question: What does the passage compare the fruit plants to in order to show their usefulness?
questions.answer: To machines or factories making sweet food.

questions.question: What example from the vine shows abundance?
questions.answer: One small branch can hold many bunches.

questions.question: What example from one grape shows careful protection?
questions.answer: Its thin skin covers it.

questions.question: What example from one grape shows planning for the future?
questions.answer: Its seeds are kept inside.

questions.question: Why is making countless grapes all over the world important in the argument?
questions.answer: Because it shows one wise plan everywhere.

questions.question: What bigger truth does that wise plan point to?
questions.answer: The Maker of grapes made the whole universe.

questions.question: Which kinds of things are said to be unable to make such fruit?
questions.answer: Blind, confused, and aimless forces.

questions.question: What can those things do instead, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They can only be used under Allah’s rule.

questions.question: When the passage speaks about many divine works together, what do they all agree on?
questions.answer: They all agree that Allah alone is the One Lord.
